dimensions.assessment: Affects all publicly traded companies subject to Securities Exchange Act disclosure rules and investors utilizing conflict mineral reports.
dimensions.evidence: publicly traded companies must annually make disclosures if certain minerals (tin, tungsten, tantalum, or gold) are necessary to the functionality or production

dimensions.assessment: Removes compliance and reporting burdens for affected corporations regarding mineral supply chain due diligence.
dimensions.evidence: Subsection (p) of section 13 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m) is hereby repealed.

dimensions.assessment: Reduces regulatory compliance costs for businesses without direct federal spending implications stated in the source.
Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and repeals section 1502 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act.
dimensions.evidence: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (12 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.) is amended--(1) by striking section 1502

dimensions.assessment: Permanent repeal of the statutory reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Subsection (p) of section 13 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m) is hereby repealed.

missing_information: Exact aggregate compliance cost savings for affected publicly traded companies
importance_detail.rationale: The bill repeals federal securities disclosure and reporting requirements related to conflict minerals from the Democratic Republic of the Congo for publicly traded companies.
